title: Customizations to coatless-quarto/pyodide
text:
This document records every change made to the upstream Quarto extension and explains how to update the extension in the future while preserving them.






Property
Value




Extension
coatless-quarto/pyodide


Pyodide runtime
0.25.0


_extension.yml version
0.0.1


Monaco Editor
0.46.0



The upstream is actively maintained; the version captured here is likely not the latest. Before updating, check the current release on GitHub.






Two lines were appended at the end of the file:
/* Set variable for backend
for Groq Server: "groq"
for flask Server: "flask"*/
globalThis.backend = "groq";

/* Set if there should be a button for feedback
with feedback button: true
without feedback button: false */
globalThis.feedback = true;
Purpose: master switches consumed by the other modified files. - backend: selects the AI provider. - feedback: enables / disables the feedback button on every cell.




The upstream file only creates the “Python interpreter: loading …” status header. All additions are inside qpyodideDisplayStartupMessage().
Added blocks (roughly lines 59–184):

Two extra <div> containers (thirdInnerDiv for Base-URL, fourthInnerDiv for API key) appended to the status area.
A <input type="text"> + <button> pair for the API key (stored in sessionStorage.groqApiKey).
A <input type="text"> + <button> pair for the Base URL (stored in sessionStorage.baseUrlInput).
A Font Awesome gear icon (fa-gear) that toggles visibility of the two input pairs.
Helper functions toggleSettings() and checkAndHideSettings().
A DOMContentLoaded listener that restores saved values from sessionStorage and hides the fields automatically when both values are present.

Also added (line 10–12): inside qpyodideSetInteractiveButtonState() the feedback buttons are enabled/disabled together with the run buttons:
document.querySelectorAll(".qpyodide-button-feedback").forEach((btn) => {
    btn.disabled = !enableCodeButton;
});




This is the largest modification. Everything is conditional on globalThis.feedback.


After the copy button, a Feedback button is created and appended to the toolbar only when feedback == true and the cell is not read-only:
if (globalThis.feedback == true) {
    var feedbackButton = document.createElement('button');
    feedbackButton.className = 'btn btn-default qpyodide-button qpyodide-button-feedback';
    feedbackButton.disabled = true;   // enabled later by qpyodideSetInteractiveButtonState
    feedbackButton.id = `qpyodide-button-feedback-${this.id}`;
    feedbackButton.textContent = "Feedback";
}
// …
if (globalThis.feedback == true && this.options['read-only'] == "false") {
    rightButtonsDiv.appendChild(feedbackButton);
}



A <div> for the AI response is inserted below the code output area:
if (globalThis.feedback == true) {
    var outputFeedbackAreaDiv = document.createElement('div');
    outputFeedbackAreaDiv.id = `qpyodide-output-feedback-area-${this.id}`;
    outputFeedbackAreaDiv.className = 'qpyodide-output-feedback-area';
    outputFeedbackAreaDiv.setAttribute('aria-live', 'assertive');
}



The handler is set up inside setupMonacoEditor() after the editor is ready. Rough flow:

Read current code from Monaco editor.
Execute code via Pyodide to capture stdout/stderr.
Assemble a prompt from three parts: system prompt + runtime output + review instructions.
Dispatch to the selected backend.

Groq path (globalThis.backend == "groq"): - Reads API key and Base URL from the DOM inputs (backed by sessionStorage). - GET {baseUrl}/models → picks "mixtral-8x7b-32768" or first available model. - POST {baseUrl}/chat/completions with messages: [{role:"system",…},{role:"user",…}]. - Renders data.choices[0].message.content into the feedback div (newlines → <br>).
Flask path (globalThis.backend == "flask"): - Fixed endpoint: http://127.0.0.1:5000/api/feedback. - Same request/response shape as Groq; no auth header.
The same logic is duplicated inside setupNewMonacoEditor() for dynamically added code blocks.





Added at the end of the file:
.qpyodide-output-feedback-area {
  background-color: darksalmon;
  color: black;
}

.qpyodide-output-feedback-area.has-content {
  padding: 10px;
}








File
Status




qpyodide.lua
unchanged from upstream


qpyodide-document-engine-initialization.js
unchanged


qpyodide-cell-initialization.js
unchanged


qpyodide-monaco-editor-init.html
unchanged


_extension.yml
unchanged









# In your project root:
quarto add coatless-quarto/pyodide
This overwrites the entire _extensions/coatless-quarto/pyodide/ directory. Say yes when prompted to update.



After updating, re-apply each section from chapter 2 above:







File to edit
What to re-apply




qpyodide-document-settings.js
Append the two globalThis.backend / globalThis.feedback lines (section 2.1).


qpyodide-document-status.js
(a) Add the querySelectorAll(".qpyodide-button-feedback") block inside qpyodideSetInteractiveButtonState. (b) Add the third/fourth inner divs + API-key UI inside qpyodideDisplayStartupMessage (section 2.2).


qpyodide-cell-classes.js
Add the feedback button creation + onclick handler in setupElement() and setupMonacoEditor(), and duplicate in setupNewMonacoEditor() (section 2.3).


qpyodide-styling.css
Append the .qpyodide-output-feedback-area rules (section 2.4).






The most common sources of breakage when updating:

Renamed functions or variables in qpyodide-cell-classes.js — search for setupElement, setupMonacoEditor, setupNewMonacoEditor in the new file and confirm they still exist with the same signatures.
Pyodide version bump — the new _extension.yml / Lua filter may point to a newer Pyodide CDN URL. The AI feedback logic itself is version-agnostic.
Monaco Editor version bump in qpyodide-monaco-editor-init.html — fine to accept as-is.




quarto preview
Verify: 1. Pyodide loads (“🟢 Ready!”). 2. Gear icon appears; entering API key + Base URL saves to sessionStorage. 3. “Feedback” button is present and enabled after Pyodide is ready. 4. Clicking Feedback executes the code and displays AI output.





Consider keeping this document version-controlled alongside the extension files. Before any update, record the upstream commit hash or release tag that was used as the baseline so the diff in step 2 can be produced mechanically if needed:
# record upstream version
cat _extensions/coatless-quarto/pyodide/_extension.yml

title: Pyodide-Feedback Quarto Minimal
text:
This is a Quarto website to showcase the use of Pyodide in a Quarto document. It is based on the Pyodide documentation and the Quarto Pyodide-Extension. Aswell as some changes to the original code of the Pyodide Extension to allow for AI Feedback.
The Extension allows you to run Python code in your Quarto documents using Pyodide. You can use it to create interactive visualizations, run data analysis, or simply execute Python code. Here are some examples of how to use the Pyodide Extension in your Quarto documents:
